newsitem.title: UK: Eurofighter slippage can be made up -UK sources.
newsitem.headline: Eurofighter slippage can be made up -UK sources.

text.p: Britain expects no serious slippage in the programme for production of the Eurofighter aircraft provided the four countries involved act quickly after the German cabinet agrees this week on finance for it.
Government sources said on Tuesday they were optimistic that a meeting of the German cabinet on Friday would approve expenditure of 23 billion marks to buy 180 of the combat jets.
Bonn coalition sources told Reuters earlier that the government had already agreed to spending more than two billion marks on the four-nation project in 1998 and 1999.

The British sources said they hoped this would be followed by German parliamentary approval in September and the signing of memoranda of understanding (MOUs) on production between Britain, Germany, Italy and Spain within a few months.
This would represent a slippage on the original programme for the aircraft since the signing of the MOUs had been scheduled for last year.
But one source said Britain believes the programme could return to schedule by early in the next century.

"There will be a little bit of slippage, but we hope it will be soaked up in the next four years," the source said. "We are hopeful that provided the MOUs are signed within the next few months this will be achievable."
Britain hopes that production of the aircraft, being undertaken by Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, British Aerospace, Spain's Casa and Italy's Alenia, can get under way early next year.
The sources said Britain was keen to acquire the Eurofighter for its air force, especially since the aircraft had performed remarkably well during flight testing.

They dismissed reports that a "few small handling deficiencies" had been found in the aircraft, saying "deficiency" was a word used by test pilots to describe anything that deviated even slightly from perfection.
